terms.gloss: a prisoner under guard; in the plural, the prisoners
terms.comment: The guarding, and so the person guarded: post-Augustan (Lewis & Short). Before then, a man held in prison is in custōdiā or in vinculīs.

terms.latin: captīvus, captīvī m.; captīva, captīvae f.
terms.comment: Classically a prisoner of war (see prisoner, of war); Levi and Bini extend it to anyone held in detention.

phrases.latin: Quemadmodum eadem catēna et custōdiam et mīlitem cōpulat
phrases.english: Just as the same chain links the prisoner and the soldier

phrases.latin: utrum per pūblicōs cīvitātium servōs, quod ūsque adhūc factum, an per mīlitēs asservāre custōdiās dēbeam
phrases.english: whether I ought to guard the prisoners with the cities’ public slaves, as has been done until now, or with soldiers

sources: Lewis & Short: custodia · Lewis & Short: captivus
Enrico Levi and Arturo Bini, Il latino come lingua viva (1937), p. 21, s.v. detenuto.
